texts: On day 300 of Year 1, the keepers of the Harbor Row together lit the lanterns of the Harbor Row at sundown.
The lanterns showed mist-light at night.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Harbor Row.
Three sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The three sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row.
The nightmoth crowd at the Harbor Row shrank.
The surviving nightmoths fled to the Hollows.
The surviving nightmoths reached the Hollows.
The three sky-cats molted during the hunt.
The nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns of the Harbor Row.

q1_issues.issue: The definite subject "The mist-light" is filled by the bare kind symbol mist_light as Agent of a specific past attracting event, but the Existential section reserves the bare class symbol for non-specific/generic objects and says a definite description picking out a specific thing takes a typed sk_ individual.

"The nightmoths" in the final sentence is resolved to sk_nightmoth_2, the surviving moths that had just fled to and reached the Hollows, rather than to the nightmoths/crowd at the Harbor Row where the threads are said to be left.

q2_gaps: Ordinal day-of-year dating in a non-Gregorian calendar ("on day 300 of Year 1"): (Day <n>) is defined as the calendar day inside a Month, with no convention for a bare day-number of a year.

Bare "together" over a DEFINITE PLURAL that is encoded as a single group witness: Coordination & plurals makes "together" force the collective form for coordinated/plural subjects, but nothing states how it interacts with the group-event + per-member distribution rule that Cardinality / Quantifiers otherwise require for a definite plural with a distributive predicate - i.e. whether "together" suppresses that rule (and, with a group subject, whether it leaves any trace at all).
review.notes: "at the Harbor Row" in sentence 8 is attached to the crowd NP as (LocatedIn sk_crowd_1 harbor_row) rather than to the hunt event, so the hunt itself gets no location; both attachments are coherent and the parse commits to one without marking the ambiguity. The collective/distributive split is otherwise handled carefully - the two "together" clauses and "gather" stay group-only, while burn / show / descend / hunt / survive / flee / reach / molt / leave each add the per-member rule.

issues.reason: Existential reserves the bare class symbol for a non-specific / generic object and bars it 'for a specific definite individual', so the definite subject 'The mist-light' of a dated past attracting event may not be filled by mist_light -- the very symbol the parse also uses kind-side in (Inheritance mist_light light).

The coherence half stands -- the survivors had just fled to and reached the Hollows while the threads sit on the Harbor Row lanterns, so the Harbor Row crowd is the better antecedent -- but the error half does not: Coreference resolves 'to the most salient compatible antecedent (gender/number agreement + recency)', which licenses the just-mentioned sk_nightmoth_2, and since those moths were at the Harbor Row before fleeing no emitted atom is false.

gaps_confirmed: Ordinal day-of-year dating in a non-Gregorian calendar ('on day 300 of Year 1'): (Day <n>) is the day-of-month slot, with no term for a bare day-number of a year.

Bare 'together' over a definite plural encoded as one group witness: the collective form is defined as one event with multiple Agent atoms, which a single group symbol cannot express, so 'together' leaves no positive trace -- its only record is the absence of the per-member distribution rule.
new_gaps: A definite mass anaphor whose antecedent entered the KB as a bare mass constant ('the lanterns produced mist-light' ... 'The mist-light attracted nightmoths'): the episodic bare-plural-object rule has no mass analogue, so the definite witness the Existential rule demands would sit unlinked to the mass that was produced and shown, and no identity link between witness and bare kind constant is licensed.
adjudication.defect_summary: Issue 0: the compliant form types the definite mass as its own individual -- (Member sk_mist_light_1 mist_light) with (Agent sk_attract_1 sk_mist_light_1) -- but nothing licenses tying that witness to the mist_light the two earlier episodic clauses stored as a bare constant, which is the gap filed above.
adjudication.notes: Unflagged by the reviewer: (Patient sk_leave_1 sk_thread_1) should be Theme -- leaving threads on the lanterns displaces them without changing them, the same test that gives 'slid the plate off the counter' a Theme. The 'at the Harbor Row' attachment onto the crowd NP is a defensible commitment rather than an unmarked ambiguity, since the next sentence repeats the same restrictor on the same NP.
